_format: Version is major.minor.build.deploy. Newest release first. Add a new entry here for every deployment; the footer shows the first entry's version.

releases.title: Struck-through scriptures, Deliver footer below the text, clean print
notes: Deliver view: the Back / Next footer now sits below everything in the section, including the theme scripture on the first page, instead of above it.
Talk Builder: when a section or point is struck through, its scriptures are crossed out and greyed with it.
Deliver view: a struck-through section folds its scriptures and its sub-points into the same accordion, so nothing from it shows until you open it.
Print: struck-through sections and points, and their scriptures, are left off the printed talk.

releases.title: Deliver view: smaller text, pinned clock, folded struck-through points
notes: Deliver view: text is a step smaller so more of a section fits on screen, and the clock with its start, pause and reset buttons is pinned at the top right, staying in view while you scroll.
Deliver view: a struck-through section or point is folded into an accordion under its crossed-out heading, so it takes one line until you open it.
Talk Builder and Deliver view: scripture text shows in orangered with a matching left edge, so verses stand apart from the talk's own lines.
Talk Builder and Deliver view: a collected line that quotes a verse stored with the talk is coloured as scripture too, and any line can be marked as scripture with the Bible button on the line.

Talk Builder: Print lays the talk out on 5 × 7 inch pages in Times New Roman, the talk text at 12 pt and the English at 8 pt, with the talk title at the top of every page and page numbers at the foot. Controls, badges, references and alternatives are left off the page; verses and scripture lines keep a rule at the left.

Deliver view: the Back / Next pager appears at the foot of each section as well as the top, and moving on scrolls back to the top of the new section. The pinned clock is translucent so it no longer hides the text beneath it, turning solid when you point at it.

releases.title: Talk Builder: images and struck-through points
notes: Talk Builder: add an image to any section with the new Add image button. The image sits among the section's lines, can be moved up and down like a line, and takes a caption. In Deliver view it shows small and right-aligned exactly where it was placed, with the lines wrapping around it, as the cue for the AV team; clicking it shows it full screen, Escape or a click closes it. Images are stored with the talk (shrunk to at most 1600 pixels) and removed with it.

Talk Builder: strike through any outline section or point you will not use, with the new strike-through button on its header. In the builder the title is crossed out and the section band turns grey; in Deliver view the whole point, its verses, lines and images, shows crossed out in light grey with a "not used" tag, so it is easy to pass over. Press the button again to use it.

releases.title: Talk Builder: article links, Hebrew Scriptures, alternatives for every line
notes: Talk Builder never contacts wol.jw.org on its own any more. Opening a talk shows only what is already stored: verses kept with the talk or in the app's Bible store, references already resolved, and library matches for a line. Anything else waits for you: "Fetch from wol.jw.org" on a verse (or one button for all missing verses), "Look up on wol.jw.org" on a reference, and "Search wol.jw.org" in a line's alternatives. Each fetch is made once and kept with the talk.

Faster pages while wol.jw.org declines requests: after a few empty answers the site is left alone for ten minutes (one probe at a time), so a talk with thirty verses no longer waits a minute for each lookup and a translation no longer sits behind them. A chapter that was declined is not asked for again for ten minutes, the Talk Builder no longer fires the same verse lookup several times at once, and the server handles requests in parallel threads so one slow lookup cannot hold up the others.

Translation on the hosted site now shows Google Translate's answer first in the Talk Builder and Conversation Builder (the neural model remains the fallback; locally MADLAD stays first). Marking a Talk Builder line as checked, or saving an edited line, stores the pair as a verified entry: a single word in the dictionary, two to five words as a verified phrase, longer text as a verified sentence, each at confidence 100 with the outline reference, so your checked translations feed the dictionary gloss and the next training run. Checking the same Chuukese again updates the entry rather than duplicating it.

Glossed Chuukese text reads as plain text again: no coloured tints on words. Phrases carry a thin dotted underline, both phrases from the phrase library and runs of dictionary words whose parts of speech form one (pronoun + noun, verb + noun, noun + adjective and so on), and hovering any word of the phrase shows the whole phrase, its English and definition. Hovering a dictionary word shows a soft cue and its gloss; clicking or tapping it (or pressing Enter on it) selects it in soft blue and pins the definition panel until the next click or Escape, so it works on phones too. Keyboard focus shows a clear outline and words are announced to screen readers. A new "Show dictionary indicators" switch in the legend adds a faint dotted underline to every dictionary word for readers who want it.

Gloss: words found in the dictionary are tinted a paler pastel green on every page (Talk Builder alternatives, Watchtower Library, articles, verses), darkening only on hover. Dictionary phrases of two to five words are underlined as one unit whether or not the text carries the same accents ("ekiek murinne" finds "ekiek múrinné"), and hovering shows the phrase, its English, its definition and each word's gloss. Example sentences from the phrase library are no longer mistaken for phrases.

Staying signed in across updates: a deployment no longer signs everyone out. The active session is kept with the user record instead of in the server's memory, so a new server build, a restart or a second replica recognises it. When a newer version is deployed, open pages show a toast within a minute: "Save and refresh" saves unsaved work first (a talk's lines, for example), then reloads the page at the same place, signed in; "What changed" opens the release notes. The Talk Builder keeps the open talk in the address, so a refresh or a shared link returns to it.

Talk Builder: printed outlines pasted without indentation (S-34 talk outlines) are now read correctly: each capitalised heading with its minutes is a section, the lines beneath it are that section's points, the "PLEASE NOTE" text shows as a subdued note under the title, the outline number sits beside the title, and the printed footer (timing reminder, copyright, form number) is left out. Talks imported earlier are fixed when reopened, with collected lines staying under their points. Sub-point headings are larger and bolder.

Talk Builder: each main section of the outline is now a tinted block with a bold violet header band showing the section number, "Section n of m", the title in large type and the time to complete as a large pill, with the line count beside it. Sub-points sit inside as white cards with a bold subheading and their own time badge. A section with no lines yet has an orange band.

Talk Builder: every collected or translated line has a "Similar on wol.jw.org and in the library" accordion. Opening it searches wol.jw.org for the line's key words and the sentence pairs already stored in the app (analysed articles, the phrase library, corrected conversation lines), and lists the closest published sentences with their English, glossed, with the citation linked and the share of words in common. Use replaces the line with the published wording; Add keeps both. Results are kept for a week; Search again refreshes them.

Talk Builder: a verse from Genesis to Malachi now shows Chuukese text from the Liebenzell Mission Paipel (1984–2001), since the New World Translation in Chuukese covers Matthew–Revelation only. Those verses carry an orange "Liebenzell Paipel, not the New World Translation" tag in the builder and in Deliver view, because the wording differs from what the talk quotes. Verses stored earlier without Chuukese are filled in when the talk is reopened.

Talk Builder: a citation that could not be resolved is no longer remembered as a failure. Earlier failed lookups (which left the citation pointing at the wol.jw.org search page) were cleared, so reopening a talk now resolves each citation through the lookup and links the article itself, with the cited paragraph and its Chuukese below the point.

Server: every request to wol.jw.org (article pages, citation lookups, Bible chapters) and every unresolved citation is now logged with the status the site answered, so a block or outage can be seen in the container logs.

releases.title: Talk Builder, Conversation Builder, content-based sentence pairing
notes: New Talk Builder page: paste or upload a talk outline (English or Chuukese, .txt/.docx/.pdf); it is parsed into points, sub-points, scriptures, publication references and time marks. Collect Chuukese lines under each point with the new Add to talk button on the Watchtower Library, Article Analysis, Sentence Analysis and Conversation Builder pages, or type lines and translate them either way. Deliver view shows one point per screen in large type with a timer against the outline's minutes. Talks are saved per user.

Talk Builder: cited verses appear under their point in both languages, Chuukese from the New World Translation on wol.jw.org (Christian Greek Scriptures only; Hebrew Scriptures chapters say so). Citation lists and abbreviations such as 2 Tim. 3:16, 17 and Rom. 12:1, 2 are expanded.

Talk Builder: publication references in a point (w12 11/1 23, w21.08 5 ¶9, g 11/12 8, wp16 2/1 5, km 5/09 3, lff lesson 16 points 4-5, bt chap. 20 ¶13-20, it-1 543) are resolved through the citation lookup on wol.jw.org. The citation in the point text is a link that opens the article at the cited place, and under the point the cited paragraph appears with its number and the key phrases of the outline marked. When the publication exists in Chuukese the Chuukese paragraph sits above it with the sentence carrying the thought marked; when it does not, the panel says so. Each Chuukese sentence can be added to the talk.

Talk Builder: scriptures and resolved articles are stored with the talk the first time they are fetched, so reopening a talk never goes back to wol.jw.org. Chuukese verse, article and collected-line text carries the same dictionary gloss as the other pages: hover a word for its meaning, grammar and definition; phrases from the articles are underlined.

New Conversation Builder page: choose a subject and statement from Truths We Love to Teach (Love People—Make Disciples) or this week's workbook part, then follow a branching conversation drawn as a flow diagram: steps are nodes, the person's answers are coloured edges, the path you walk lights up, and a side panel holds the lines for the selected step. Lines quoted from the brochure are authentic; authored lines are machine translated, marked, and can be corrected in place. Correcting a line edits both languages, the other side suggested by back-translation, and corrected lines join the training data. Conversations are saved per user.

Article Analysis: Chuukese and English sentences are paired by content (scripture citations, numbers, list markers, question marks, dictionary glosses and length) instead of by position. Sentences the translator reordered, split or merged now line up, and paragraphs are matched even when one edition has an extra footnote. A footnote letter after a full stop no longer glues two English sentences together, and study-question labels such as 2. (a) and (b) stay with the question they introduce.

Watchtower Library, Sentence Analysis and Translation Game: the English for a hit is found with the same content-based pairing, so a reordered or merged sentence is matched and a question paragraph is no longer confused with its neighbour when the editions' paragraph ids drift.

Article Analysis: Re-analyze fetches the article afresh instead of returning the stored copy; sentences are numbered paragraph.sentence (1.1, 1.2, 2.1 …) and each paragraph opens with a large paragraph number.
Basic users can now open the Translation Game; every link above the divider in the left navigation is available to all roles.

Saved searches, article analyses and sentence analyses are now per user: each person's sidebar lists only what they saved. The underlying content is shared, so an article or search another user already pulled is served from the stored copy instead of fetching wol.jw.org again.

Dictionary: 1,247 headwords that were stored with a suffix hyphen (wis-ach) are now whole words (wisach) with the stem, suffix and suffix meaning recorded, so sentence analysis no longer reports them as missing.

releases.title: First numbered release
notes: Version number and this release notes page added to the site footer.
Left navigation reordered: Word Lookup now sits above AI Translation, and Translation Game follows Article Analysis.

AI Translator: Helsinki-NLP models retrained on 45,000 Chuukese–English pairs, including sentences distilled from the larger MADLAD-400 model. Translations in both directions are markedly more accurate than the previous model.
Sentence and Article Analysis rebuilt on the Watchtower Online Library dictionary layer, with source lookup and saved analyses.
Translation Game: clues, glosses, phrase matching and saved-match colours.
Admin: translation review queue and dictionary de-duplication.
AI Training page: automatic retraining is switched off on the hosted site (it has no GPU); models are trained offline and uploaded. Manual runs remain available.
Training pipeline: memory-guarded local training, checkpoint resume, and retry on database throttling.
